subject: Post-demo checklist: procurement readiness, PO vs card & marketplace billing
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
To: Sana Patel <sana@brightpath.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@brightpath.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference, marissa.cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo checklist: procurement readiness, PO vs card & marketplace billing

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a short procurement checklist so we can confirm the right commercial path (PO vs card) and whether marketplace billing is an option for you.

What we covered:
- Technical fit: model latency targets and data isolation OK for your pilot.
- Usage profile: bursty demo traffic, expected steady state ~2M tokens/month if pilot expands.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC private deployment discussed; you requested vendor onboarding packet.

Procurement checklist / questions for your AP team:
1) Preferred payment method: do you require a Purchase Order (PO) / Net30 terms, or can you process via corporate card (immediate payment)?
2) Vendor setup: does your team require W9, banking details, vendor risk questionnaire (I can provide a one-page vendor packet)?
3) Marketplace interest: would you prefer procurement via AWS/Azure marketplace (simpler for card billing / consolidated invoicing) or direct Redwood invoicing?
4) Timeline: when would procurement need the SOW/contract to kick off vendor onboarding? Typical vendor onboarding is 4–8 weeks once paperwork is complete.

Attached is the draft SOW (BrightPath_SOW_v1.pdf) and a small vendor onboarding packet to share with AP (vendor_onboarding_packet.zip).

Next suggested steps:
- You: confirm payment preference (PO vs card) and whether marketplace is acceptable for SaaS billing.
- Rishi: I’ve looped you for pricing/contract alignment in case they need an accelerated approval or a pre-approved quote for PO.
- Marissa: please hold a standard PO-ready quote with net30 and an alternate card-pricing line so we can move quickly depending on AP preference.

Happy to hop on a short call with AP if that speeds things up.

Best,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Email: olga.petrov@redwood.inference | M: (415) 555-0143

Attachments: BrightPath_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 24 KB), vendor_onboarding_packet.zip (ZIP, 180 KB)

From: Sana Patel <sana@brightpath.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@brightpath.ai>, procure@brightpath.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo checklist: procurement readiness, PO vs card & marketplace billing

Thanks Olga — great demo. Short answers from AP side (copied):

- Preferred payment: Our default is PO / Net30 for any new SaaS vendor over $5k/mo. We can use card for initial POC if vendor accepts credit card and can produce a monthly invoice.
- Vendor setup: AP requires W9, vendor W-9 (we'll need your tax ID), completed vendor risk questionnaire, and copies of SOC2 attestation.
- Marketplace: We prefer to procure via our cloud marketplace when possible (AWS Marketplace). That can allow consolidated billing to our cloud account, but it depends on whether Redwood can offer list pricing through marketplace or via a reseller.
- Timeline: If we decide to go PO, internal lead time is ~3 weeks to issue PO once vendor packet is in our system. If card, we can start next week.

Tom is our procurement lead on this; I’ll let him coordinate next steps for the vendor packet.

—Sana
Sana Patel
Head of Product, BrightPath AI
sana@brightpath.ai

Folks — forwarding BrightPath's AP responses. TL;DR: they prefer PO/Net30 for production, but can take card for the POC. They want W9, SOC2, and a vendor questionnaire. Marketplace (AWS) is preferred if we can support it, but that adds contracting complexity (reseller or marketplace listing).

Questions / asks for this thread:
- Rishi: can you produce a PO-ready quote (Net30) with a parallel card-eligible invoice option for the POC? If marketplace pricing is materially different, flag that and we can discuss margins with finance.
- Marissa: please prepare the vendor packet bundle — W9, SOC2 attestation link, standard MSAs and a short onboarding checklist. I'll attach our standard SOW and ask legal to prepare a quick PO-friendly addendum.
- Do we want to offer a marketplace path as a contingency? If yes, who owns that operationally (channel/partnership)?

I'll wait for your draft quote and vendor packet before replying to Tom (procure@brightpath.ai). If it's faster, I'm happy to join their AP call to walk through requirements.

Thanks,
Olga
